payload.goal: A driven run must not saturate the operator's machine: sessions and --verify run at bounded parallelism and lower priority, a verify timeout reaps its whole process tree, and load-induced test timeouts do not reopen tasks into a relaunch loop.

payload.text: Audit 2026-09-29 (14 cores / 24 GB, live run linked-context pid 36300). F1 The driver is NOT the load: node driver 31 MB, ~0% CPU; watchers are 2s byte-scans; stream-json parse keeps only counters + a bounded stderr tail. Per session: claude 70-140 MB + sofar mcp 30 MB. F2 The load is the test work a run multiplies. Measured on main: `npx vitest run` peak 3.0 GB / 5.3 cores / 36 procs / 48s (vitest.config.ts sets no maxWorkers, so the unit project forks cores-1 = 13 workers); `cargo test -q --workspace` 1.1 GB / 3.7 cores / 183s (no -j cap); `npm run -s typecheck` 0.6 GB / 2 cores. The session under drive ran the full suite >=4 times itself before the driver's --verify ran it again. F3 Feedback loop, observed: linked-context 1.1 verify failed (64.6s, exit 1) on vitest default 5000ms testTimeout (attribution-cache.test.ts:96, conformance repo.session-start) — load-induced, not code. The driver reopened the task and launched a fresh session told to make the command pass -> more full-suite runs under the same load, up to --max-sessions 10. F4 driver/verify.ts runVerification uses spawnSync(shell:true, timeout): the event loop blocks for up to --verify-timeout (1800s here) so --stop is not seen mid-verify, and on timeout only the shell is signalled — vitest forks / cargo test binaries are not in a group the driver kills, so they can orphan. Not observed live. F5 Nothing lowers the priority of sessions or verify (no nice / taskpolicy), so they compete with the operator's foreground at equal priority. Context at audit time: an orphaned `tsc --noEmit` in ~/IO/splen (pid 4843, 3.6 GB, 196% CPU, 36 min, parent npm exec reparented to launchd) and two handoff-bench rounds running `next build` also loaded the box — not sofar. Aside: main has 5 real vitest failures (fold-parity FP-01 x3, digest-cache Rust v3 bytes x2) — assertion diffs, not timeouts.

payload.next_action: On operator go-ahead, plan drive-load from note 01M3PCDC: nice/taskpolicy the session group and verify, cap vitest maxWorkers and cargo jobs, async verify in its own process group with group kill, retry a timeout-only verify fail once before reopening.
payload.summary: Audited sofar drive resource use against a live run. The driver process is cheap; the machine is saturated by unbounded-parallel test runs that a run repeats, and load-induced 5s test timeouts turn verify failures into relaunch loops. Findings F1-F5 in note 01M3PCDC27TWJFPN66Z3WW1W43. No code changed; fixes await operator go-ahead.
